PullRequest.Title: sessions: Align Agents Window hovers and instant-hover groups

## Summary

Apply the hover guidance from #343505 to the Agents Window so widget boundaries do not introduce extra delays between related controls.

- Share instant-hover delegates across adjacent title-bar toolbars, composer controls, and automation pickers, including custom action-view items.
- Group related artifact buttons, tabs, suggestions, and comparison controls using stable lifecycle group IDs.
- Replace native DOM tooltips with custom hovers while preserving accessible labels and disabled explanations.
- Pair element placement with pointers, use mouse placement for simple list tooltips, and place rich list hovers to the side.
- Add regression coverage for shared delegates, independent groups, custom tooltip content, pointer styling, and actual initial-delay/instant-transition behavior.

## Validation

Validated after rebasing onto current `main`, using Node.js 24.22.0:

- `fnm exec --using v24.22.0 npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed.
- `fnm exec --using v24.22.0 npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `git diff --name-only -z origin/main...HEAD -- '*.ts' | xargs -0 fnm exec --using v24.22.0 npm run eslint --` — passed for all 48 changed TypeScript files.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.
- Focused Electron unit tests below — **1,574 passed, 1 existing pending test**. The timing regression verifies no hover before 500 ms and an immediate transition to an adjacent target in the same group.

Full-window manual UI verification and integration/smoke suites were not run.

For a manual check, hover a title-bar action or composer picker until its tooltip appears, then move between neighboring controls: the first tooltip should respect `workbench.hover.delay`, subsequent related tooltips should appear immediately, and element-anchored hovers should have pointers. Also check the nested-session folder/branch controls, artifact section buttons, and simple versus rich sessions-list tooltips.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agents window startup and construction of title bars, composer controls, banners, and automation form controls
Scenarios.CriticalPath: DOM/control construction and registration of shared hover delegates/listeners complete synchronously before each surface is interactive; hover widget creation and content rendering remain off the startup critical path until pointer or focus interaction.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of persistent controls on the visible surface, realistically tens; sharing delegates reduces delegate cardinality across adjacent toolbars and picker groups.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI-thread construction; each surface owns one shared instant-hover delegate where grouping was added, with no asynchronous fan-out or work queue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Delegates persist for the owning widget/dialog and are reused warm across adjacent controls; no data cache, cache miss, negative cache, or coalescing behavior is changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from tracing createInstantHoverDelegate, WorkbenchHoverDelegate, setupManagedHover, and owning DisposableStore lifetimes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact listener setup cost is unmeasured, but control cardinality is bounded and no heavyweight content is eagerly created.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: added listener/delegate setup is bounded, disposed with its owner, and hover widgets are lazily created on interaction.

Scenarios.Scenario: Moving the pointer among grouped title-bar, composer, automation, artifact, comparison, and prompt-option controls
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the initial configured delay, pointer movement invokes the existing hover service on the UI thread; same-group transitions can use zero delay, but only one top-level hover stack is active.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One hovered target at a time among a bounded adjacent control group; cost scales with pointer transitions, not total repository/session data.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Event-driven and effectively serialized by the hover service/current-hover state; no concurrent subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The shared delegate retains only recent hide time and current hover disposables for its owner; hover identity/current state prevents duplicate top-level creation, and disposal clears listeners.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from HoverService and WorkbenchHoverDelegate call paths plus changed lifecycle grouping.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Rendering cost depends on hover content, but the diff primarily changes placement/grouping and does not add expensive content generation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff changes hover timing and placement without increasing expensive-work cardinality or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rendering and recycling session-list, AI customization, and extension-list rows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Visible row rendering synchronously registers a delayed-hover listener/map entry; the actual hover DOM is created only if the user hovers. Row rendering itself does not cross an external boundary.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is the number of rendered/recycled visible rows, not the full session, customization, or extension collection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI-thread virtualized list/tree rendering; row templates clear elementDisposables before reuse and dispose them when templates are destroyed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Virtualized templates are reused; hover registrations are replaced through elementDisposables, and HoverService map entries are removed on disposal. No cold/warm backend cache behavior changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from renderer lifecycle and HoverService disposal tracing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Visible-row counts and rerender frequency vary, but registrations are bounded and equivalent delayed-hover machinery already existed on session rows.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: replacing native or element-positioned tooltips with custom mouse hovers adds bounded per-visible-row setup with explicit cleanup, not unbounded retention or collection-wide eager rendering.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening and interacting with a mobile picker sheet or mobile title-bar changes pill
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Sheet construction and changes-pill render update tooltip strings and register managed/delayed hover handlers synchronously; popup rendering remains deferred until hover/focus.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A small bounded set of sheet header actions and one changes pill; changes aggregation remains the pre-existing linear scan of changed files and is not increased by hover setup.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI-thread interaction with one shared delegate per sheet and one delayed hover for the pill; no asynchronous burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The sheet-scoped delegate and handlers are disposed on close; tooltip text is held only for the owning component lifetime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from changed shell construction and component disposal ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Mobile action counts vary but are structurally small; no evidence of large dynamic header collections.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: custom hover setup replaces native titles with bounded lifecycle-owned listeners and does not add external work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 48 changed files and all diff pages. Traced hover delegate creation, delayed/managed hover allocation, virtualized row reuse, disposal ownership, and UI critical paths. No actionable diff-introduced performance regression or evidenced regression fix was found.
